arxiv-2104-01252.title: Autonomous Driving Data Chain & Interfaces
arxiv-2104-01252.creator: Benjamin Kahl
arxiv-2104-01252.description: Abstract Recent developments in autonomous driving technology have proven that map data may be used, not only for general routing purposes, but also for to enhance and complement common sensor data. This document reviews the most commonly used interfaces and formats at each step of a self-healing map data chain.

arxiv-2105-05572.title: Spontaneous edge corner currents in s + i ​ s s+is superconductors and time reversal symmetry breaking surface states
arxiv-2105-05572.creator: Andrea Benfenati, Egor Babaev
arxiv-2105-05572.description: Abstract We present a study of the basic microscopic model of an s s -wave superconductor with frustrated interband interaction. When frustration is strong, such an interaction gives raise to a s + i ​ s s+is state. This is a s s -wave superconductor that spontaneously breaks time reversal symmetry.

arxiv-2105-11713.title: The Topology of Randomized Symmetry-Breaking Distributed Computing
arxiv-2105-11713.creator: Pierre Fraigniaud, Ran Gelles, Zvi Lotker
arxiv-2105-11713.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Pierre Fraigniaud, Ran Gelles, Zvi Lotker. Studying distributed computing through the lens of algebraic topology has been the source of many significant breakthroughs during the last two decades, especially in the design of lower bounds or impossibility results for deterministic algorithms.

arxiv-2207-07751.title: MARLAS: Multi Agent Reinforcement Learning for cooperated Adaptive Sampling
arxiv-2207-07751.creator: Lishuo Pan ∗1,2, Sandeep Manjanna ∗1,3, and M. Ani Hsieh 1
arxiv-2207-07751.description: Abstract The multi-robot adaptive sampling problem aims at finding trajectories for a team of robots to efficiently sample the phenomenon of interest within a given endurance budget of the robots. In this paper, we propose a robust and scalable approach using Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for cooperated Adaptive Sampling (MARLAS) of quasi-static environmental processes.

arxiv-2302-05784.title: On the number of edges of cyclic subgroup graphs of finite groups
arxiv-2302-05784.creator: Marius Tărnăuceanu
arxiv-2302-05784.description: Abstract In this note, we show that among finite nilpotent groups of a given order or finite groups of a given odd order, the cyclic group of that order has the minimum number of edges in its cyclic subgroup graph. We also conjecture that this holds for arbitrary finite groups. MSC2000 : Primary 20D60; Secondary 20D15, 05C07.

arxiv-2302-12861.title: Quark mass dependence of the low-lying charmed mesons at one loop in HH χ \chi PT
arxiv-2302-12861.creator: F. Gil-Domínguez, R. Molina
arxiv-2302-12861.description: Abstract We study the light and heavy quark mass dependence of the low-lying charmed mesons in the framework of one-loop HH χ \chi PT. The low energy constants are determined by analyzing the available lattice data from different LQCD simulations. Model selection tools are implemented to determine the relevant parameters as required by data with a higher precision.

Social interactions are hard to explain because of their uncertainty.

arxiv-2309-13083.description: Abstract Permutation Entropy ( PE \PE ) is a powerful nonlinear analysis technique for univariate time series. Recently, Permutation Entropy for Graph signals ( PE_G \PEG ) has been proposed to extend PE to data residing on irregular domains. However, PE_G \PEG is limited as it provides a single value to characterise a whole graph signal.

arxiv-2404-00067.description: Abstract Color Doppler echocardiography enables visualization of blood flow within the heart. However, the limited frame rate impedes the quantitative assessment of blood velocity throughout the cardiac cycle, thereby compromising a comprehensive analysis of ventricular filling. Concurrently, deep learning is demonstrating promising outcomes in post-processing of echocardiographic data for various applications.

arxiv-2404-08373.title: Polarisable soft solvent models with applications in dissipative particle dynamics
arxiv-2404-08373.creator: Silvia Chiacchiera, Patrick B. Warren, Andrew J. Masters, Michael A. Seaton
arxiv-2404-08373.description: Abstract We critically examine a broad class of explicitly polarisable soft solvent models aimed at applications in dissipative particle dynamics. We obtain the dielectric permittivity using the fluctuating box dipole method in linear response theory, and verify the models in relation to several test cases including demonstrating ion desorption from an oil-water interface due to image charge effects.

arxiv-2410-14094.title: The emergence of Newtonian mechanics from the inhomogeneity of an ensemble
arxiv-2410-14094.creator: Hong Yuan (袁红), C.P. Sun (孙昌璞)
arxiv-2410-14094.description: Abstract To address the observation of Max Born (M. Born 1969) that the Newton’s second law can emerge from a purely statistical perspective, we derive the evolution equation about the statistical distribution for dilute gas based solely on statistical principles, without invoking Newtonian mechanics, and then obtain the equations of motion for individual particles.

arxiv-2410-19088.title: Graded transcendental functions: an application to four-point amplitudes with one off-shell leg
arxiv-2410-19088.creator: Thomas Gehrmann, Johannes Henn, Petr Jakubčík, Jungwon Lim, Cesare Carlo Mella, Nikolaos Syrrakos, Lorenzo Tancredi, and William J. Torres Bobadilla
arxiv-2410-19088.description: Abstract Several recent works have demonstrated the powerful algebraic simplifications that can be achieved for scattering amplitudes through a systematic grading of transcendental quantities. We develop these concepts to construct a minimal basis of functions tailored to a scattering amplitude in a general way.

pmc-11543051.creator: Yuchun Li, Linlin Wang, Jingyu Wang, Yaping Xin, Xiaodong Lyu
pmc-11543051.description: Background and ObjectiveThe bone marrow microenvironment is closely related to normal hematopoiesis and hematologic tumors. Adipocytes are an important part of the bone marrow microenvironment, in which they can release free fatty acids (FFAs) through lipolysis and secrete adipocytokines, etc., and participate in normal hematopoiesis, which is closely related to the occurrence and treatment of hematological tumors.

pmc-12597853.title: Exploring the boundaries of Niemann-Pick disease type A/B: a report of a case and review of literature
pmc-12597853.creator: Mohamed El-mezayen, Abdelrahman M Tawfik, Abdalla M Hadhoud, Virginia M Gerges, Mohamed H Afify
pmc-12597853.description: BackgroundAcid sphingomyelinase deficiency (ASMD), also known as Niemann-Pick disease types A and B, is a rare autosomal recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by SMPD1 mutations. It is characterized by sphingomyelin accumulation and a broad clinical spectrum ranging from severe neurodegeneration in type A to a milder visceral phenotype in type B.

pmc-12607552.title: Ovariectomy Enhances Carcass Performance and Meat Quality by Modulating Muscle Development and Lipid Metabolism in Wuding Hens
pmc-12607552.creator: Le Zhang, Xiaoqi Xu, Wenbin Dao, Yongwang Miao
pmc-12607552.description: Simple SummaryEstrogen is an important hormone that shapes muscle growth and function, but its role in female chickens has not been fully clarified. To address this, we used Wuding hens, a traditional Chinese breed, and surgically removed the ovaries to establish an estrogen-deficient model.

pmc-12965852.title: Reprogramming Skin Aging: A Regenerative and Epigenetic Perspective on Cutaneous Longevity
pmc-12965852.creator: Diala Haykal, Michael Gold, Edward Lain, Jeremy Green, Patricia K. Farris
pmc-12965852.description: Today, patients increasingly seek interventions that not only enhance appearance, but also preserve the vitality, structure, and biological performance of their skin over time. This shift reflects the evolving science of longevity, which distinguishes between lifespan, the number of years a person lives, and healthspan, the number of years lived in good health, free from disease and functional decline.

pmc-13118383.title: Esculetin Attenuates Inflammation and Fibrosis to Prevent AKI-to-CKD Transition in Adenine-Induced Renal Injury by Inhibiting the EGFR/SRC/PI3K/AKT/NF-κB Signaling Axis
pmc-13118383.creator: Jianglong Chen, Bin Xia, Rujie Zhou, Yunfei Cui, Yu Zhu, Meijia Chen, Jinhua Su, Jinhui Wang, Guang Li
pmc-13118383.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is characterized by irreversible structural damage and functional deterioration of the kidneys. Esculetin (ES), with its anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and immunomodulatory activities, shows potential in delaying renal function decline. This study aimed to investigate the protective effect of ES on adenine-induced CKD in mice and its underlying molecular mechanism, with a focus on its role in preventing the transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to CKD.

pmc-13266228.title: Oncofertility outcomes in early-onset patients with non-breast solid malignancies: a systematic review
pmc-13266228.creator: Natali Shirron, Andrea Boutros, Ithai Waldhorn, Jubran Boulos, Matteo Lambertini, Irit Ben-Aharon
pmc-13266228.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryBackgroundThe combination of a rising incidence of early-onset cancer and the trend towards delayed parenthood has made the impact of treatments on fertility highly significant. While there is abundant evidence on oncofertility outcomes of anti-cancer treatment protocols used in people with breast cancer and haematological malignancies, data regarding gonadal toxicity and fertility preservation in young people with other cancers are lacking.

pmc-13432216.title: Cone-beam computed tomography-guided biomimetic management of extensive internal inflammatory resorption with histopathologic correlation
pmc-13432216.creator: Z. K. Sincy, Shiji Dinakaran, Keerthana Surendran, C. Leela Krishnan
pmc-13432216.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Internal inflammatory resorption is an uncommon pathologic condition characterized by progressive loss of intraradicular dentin due to clastic activity within inflamed pulp tissue. Early diagnosis is challenging because clinical symptoms are often absent until significant structural damage occurs. This case report describes the diagnosis and conservative management of extensive internal inflammatory resorption in a maxillary central incisor of a 30-year-old male patient. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) was used to confirm the extent of the lesion and differentiate it from external resorption.

pmc-13515003.title: VLM-Assisted Routing and HU-Traceable DICOM Adaptation for Lumbar CT HU Measurement: A Deployment-Oriented Pilot Technical Evaluation
pmc-13515003.creator: Zhe-Yu Ye, Jun-Mu Peng, Tamotsu Kamishima
pmc-13515003.description: Automated lumbar computed tomography (CT) Hounsfield unit (HU) measurement can support opportunistic osteoporosis screening, but heterogeneous Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) inputs often disrupt automated workflows before measurement. We evaluated a local Qwen2.5-VL-7B vision-language model (VLM)-assisted front end for suitability routing, input planning, and HU-traceable DICOM-derived field-of-view/orientation adaptation upstream of an unchanged single-slice lumbar CT HU workflow.

pmc-13524717.title: Highlights of the 2025 American Joint Replacement Registry Annual Report
pmc-13524717.creator: David Novikov, Niall Cochrane, James I Huddleston, Brett R Levine, Anna Cohen-Rosenblum
pmc-13524717.description: The 2025 American Joint Replacement Registry Annual Report includes 4.6 million hip and knee arthroplasty procedures, with 4,434,668 validated cases, representing a 20% increase from the prior report. Registry participation continues to expand, with contributions from over 5000 surgeons and 1200 institutions, including an increasing submission of patient-reported outcome measures.

pmc-13607962.title: The Diversity of Hymenoptera on Pummelo (Citrus maxima (Burm.) Merr.)
pmc-13607962.creator: Caihong Zhang, Xiangzeng Xu, Xiaojiao Zhang, Qinlin Deng, Xue Li, Shide Gao
pmc-13607962.description: Simple SummaryWasps and ants help control agricultural pests, while bees pollinate crops. Together, these insects provide essential services that support healthy farming ecosystems. However, little is known about these insects in tropical pummelo orchards in China. This study surveyed these insects in pummelo orchards in Xishuangbanna, Yunnan Province, over one year.
